## 固定收益市場主線

亞洲科技股隔夜崩跌，市場對人工智慧融資的疑慮加深，資金轉向公債，帶動10月15日美國公債大漲。10年期殖利率下降12.74個基點至5.058%，2年期僅下降5.93個基點至4.7382%。即使9月生產者物價與零售銷售均優於預期，中長天期公債仍領漲。投資人一方面評估AI投資與成長可能受創的風險，另一方面也面對聯準會持續緊縮的壓力。

美股大幅收復失土，並未扭轉資金買進債券的走勢。標普500指數收紅，Nvidia執行長黃仁勳的談話也協助CoreWeave股價由跌轉漲，但信用市場的疑慮未見同等程度的緩解：CoreWeave的5年期違約保障成本盤中創新高，科技業以外的個別借款人也遭遇劇烈的債券重估。市政債跟隨公債上漲，美國高收益債整體利差則小幅收窄。這一天，利率部位強勁反彈，但投資人對各家公司償債、再融資及擴大借款的能力，仍有明顯區別。

## 物價與支出強於預期，美債仍大漲

美國開盤前，美債已走出大部分漲幅。南韓Kospi指數重挫近8%，較9月高點累計下跌約21%；三星電子與SK海力士各跌逾9%，市場一度暫停交易20分鐘。外資週四賣出$27億韓股，10月累計賣超超過$100億。日本日經225指數下跌近5%，台灣加權指數下跌3.4%，外資賣超創紀錄的NT$3,026億，約合$93億。

半導體投資占有重要地位的亞洲經濟體，因而直接受到AI融資疑慮衝擊。美債各期限殖利率盤中一度下降12至15個基點；美國生產者物價與零售銷售增幅高於預期，僅短暫打斷漲勢。富國銀行策略師Angelo Manolatos認為，避險需求與AI疑慮主導行情；德意志銀行Steven Zeng則指出，投資人已越過當前強勁數據，開始考量若產業問題深化，經濟可能承受的壓力。

收盤殖利率曲線反映中長天期需求較強。5年期殖利率下降10.94個基點至4.8775%，30年期下降11.75個基點至5.4056%；2年與10年期利差收窄6.81個基點至31.98個基點，2年與30年期利差縮減5.82個基點至66.74個基點。本週10年與30年期殖利率分別累計下降16.88及19.45個基點，2年期卻只下降1.95個基點。投資人增加存續期間曝險之際，政策預期仍限制2年期公債的表現。

抗通膨債券更清楚揭示這波漲勢的來源。10年期實質殖利率下降9.65個基點至2.7283%，占名目殖利率降幅的大部分；10年期損益兩平通膨率則下降3.09個基點至2.3297%。不過，10年期名目殖利率本月仍上升7個基點，其中實質殖利率上升12.13個基點，通膨補償下降5.13個基點抵銷部分升幅。週四行情減輕了偏高的實質借款成本，尚未抹去本月升幅。

9月生產者物價報告仍為聯準會帶來另一組強勁通膨數據。整體PPI月增1.3%，高於市場預期的0.5%，前值則上修為0.5%；年增率由修正後的5.6%加速至6.3%，也超過預期的5.3%。核心PPI月增0.7%，高於預期的0.3%及前值0.2%；年增率達5%，相較市場預期4.4%，前值則修正為4.8%。

排除食品、能源與貿易服務的PPI月增0.5%，高於前值0.3%；年增率由修正後的4.8%升至5%。漲價範圍廣泛，顯示壓力並不限於能源。不過，Bloomberg的美債報導指出，經濟學家用來推估聯準會偏好之消費通膨指標的PPI分項，整體上促使他們下修9月PCE通膨預測。PCE將在10月28日政策決議隔日公布，因此PPI整體數字與其對消費通膨的不同含義，格外關鍵。

9月零售銷售月增0.8%，明顯高於預期0.3%，前值則修正為增加1.3%，其中汽油支出推升了整體表現。Annex Wealth Management的Brian Jacobsen認為，高油價正排擠其他消費；eToro的Bret Kenwell也強調，名目銷售尚未經通膨調整。富國投資研究所Gary Schlossberg預期消費支出將放緩，但AI投資帶來的直接與間接支撐可限制減速幅度。令市場不安的同一輪投資循環，在這項經濟判斷中仍是重要支柱。

勞動市場尚無突然惡化的明顯跡象。截至10月10日當週初領失業救濟金人數為19.9萬人，市場預期20萬人，前值修正為19.8萬人。截至10月3日當週續領人數由修正後的171.4萬人降至171萬人，符合預期。亞特蘭大聯準銀行GDPNow對第3季成長率的估計維持3.6%。

地區製造業調查則出現明顯分歧。10月紐約州製造業指數由7.60躍升至25.50，遠高於預期10.3；費城製造業指數卻由37.8降至20.9，不及預期28.4。費城新訂單指數從29.2降至4.3，就業指數由11.8降至9.1，支付價格指數由48.60降至43.20；未來營運狀況指數從52.9降至33.0，資本支出意願也由37.10降至34.90。製造業仍在擴張，但費城的訂單與展望明顯轉弱，與紐約加速成長形成對照。

8月企業存貨增加0.4%，符合預期，前值上修為0.9%；不含汽車的零售存貨持平，低於預期增加0.1%及前值0.8%。連同製造業調查的分歧，這些數據顯示，不能將名目消費增強一概視為全體經濟需求同步轉強。

路透在這段期間刊出的訪問中，舊金山聯準銀行總裁Mary Daly於週三表示，進一步升息的可能性較高，但無須立即行動，時機仍待討論。依Bloomberg美債報導，週四交換市場仍預期年底前再升息一次，其中10月升息機率約30%；後續緊縮幅度的預期則有所降溫，市場完全反映的額外25個基點升息次數已少於三次。

市政債也加入漲勢。紐約時間下午4時，指標10年期市政債殖利率下降16個基點至3.74%，創2025年4月以來最大單日降幅；30年期下降15個基點至4.97%。CIBC Private Wealth Management的Chris Lanouette將長天期買盤與資金撤出股票連結，DWS的Chad Farrington則另提到ETF持續淨流入。美國財政部擴大後的買回計畫，週四也在10至20年期區間買進上限金額$60億。

美股收盤時，標普500已回升至上漲0.33%，那斯達克100僅跌0.05%；半導體股仍跌0.88%，本週累計下跌8.26%。美元指數下跌0.53%至102.004，黃金期貨上漲1.82%至每盎司$4,182.80。能源價格帶來的緩解並不一致：布蘭特原油下跌0.41%至每桶$105.62，WTI則上漲2.60%至$97.56。EIA公布原油庫存減少855.7萬桶，遠大於預期減少30萬桶；汽油庫存卻增加351.8萬桶，與預期減少50萬桶相反。債市反彈之際，燃料供需仍不均衡。

## CoreWeave股價反彈，信用壓力未退

CoreWeave最重要的供應商出面力挺，協助股價回穩，但其信用保障在週四仍持續變貴。依ICE Data Services，5年期違約保障成本盤中最多上升74.5個基點至1,194.5個基點，創歷史新高；當時交換價格隱含的未來五年違約機率超過60%，較前一天報導的逾50%進一步惡化。

現券也再度承壓，個別券種表現有所分歧。紐約時間上午11時，2031年到期、票息9%的債券下跌約2.5美分至面額每美元80.75美分，殖利率15.3%；2030年到期、票息9.25%的債券下跌約0.75美分至約86美分，殖利率14.3%。另一期2031年到期、票息9.75%的債券卻微漲0.125美分至80.625美分。公司借款涵蓋不同結構與票息，各券反映的融資成本也不盡相同。

黃仁勳在斯德哥爾摩為CoreWeave辯護，表示其財務實力正改善，資金成本也在下降。Nvidia既是主要供應商，也是持股約10%的第二大股東。CoreWeave股價抹去先前跌幅，收漲5.9%至$69.69；黃仁勳並稱Nvidia無須提供財務後盾。他的判斷，與當天投資人面對的困境債券殖利率及創紀錄保障成本形成反差。

龐大融資需求，使市場對這種分歧格外敏感。華爾街估計公司今年全年營收達$129億，明年將再翻倍以上，但債務已超過$400億，未來五年面臨大量還款。自由現金流缺口持續擴大，分析師預期今年虧損超過$25億。CoreWeave則主張，已簽約的積壓訂單足以支持有擔保與無擔保債務償付，無須依賴客戶續約或將擔保資產重新出租。爭議核心在於快速擴張的價值與融資能否支應既有義務，而供應商也對公司的成功具有財務利益。

其他新融資計畫顯示，基礎建設仍在推進。知情人士表示，Blue Owl旗下Stack Infrastructure本週已委任安排銀行、承銷商及簿記行，擬籌措一筆5年期A$86億、約合$60億貸款，支應墨爾本資料中心計畫，可能成為區內同業最大融資案之一。高盛9月報告估計，今年全球AI相關債券發行量已達約$5,780億，超大規模雲端業者占40%。

企業營運數據也比市場反應所呈現的情況更強。台積電提出優於預期的營收展望，儘管當季毛利率略低於分析師預估。Anthropic向潛在投資人表示，第3季營收達$168億，並已實現調整後獲利；另一則報導則指出其自由現金流為正，毛利率達85%。公司正準備最快於11月9日正式展開IPO行銷，爭取年底前上市。投資人擔心的是成長速度放慢，而當下已有相當規模的實際營收與需求。

相關曝險也遠超過雲端營運商。Blackstone總裁Jon Gray表示，AI投資是公司核心，其資料中心資產已達$2,000億；布局包括與Google合資的雲端事業、OpenAI股權、以Broadcom與Nvidia晶片作擔保的貸款，以及電廠與冷卻設備投資。週四晚間報導引述Gartner分析指出，若AI基礎建設投資超過相關營收所能支撐的規模，$3.5兆支出最快可能於2030年面臨減損。大型投資人持續投入資本的同時，這項評估也對未來資產的經濟效益提出疑問。

亞洲對這輪支出的依賴，是重要的經濟差異。IMF將2026年區域成長預測上調至4.8%，部分歸因於AI投資，並預期明年放緩至4.4%；但也警告，投資或估值若出現修正，科技供應鏈核心經濟體將受到特別嚴重的衝擊。電子業其他領域已承受成本壓力：IDC指出，記憶體成本一年上漲約350%，全球智慧型手機上季出貨量因而創紀錄衰退22%，預期至少到2028年才會恢復成長。即使基礎建設支出尚未萎縮，運算投入品的強勁需求已推高其他使用者的成本。

## 信用表現分化，借款人爭取新條件

AI以外，FMC是當天信用市場重估最劇烈的個案之一。這家農用化學品生產商宣布大幅調整定價後，其2031年到期投資級債券殖利率升至約10.5%。需求疲弱、經銷商持有的高價存貨及學名產品競爭，使補庫訂單遲遲未至。公司擬縮小美國售價總額與淨額的差距，改變先訂高價、再提供大額回扣的模式，並調降巴西、阿根廷與加拿大售價。

FMC估計第3季將承受$6.25億至$6.75億衝擊，調整後EBITDA虧損$5.10億至$5.65億。公司預期截至9月30日仍符合財務契約，但計畫未來一年與貸款銀行討論進一步修改條款，為定價改造取得彈性。股價一度重挫40%。Benjamin Theurer率領的巴克萊分析師團隊認為，營運與財測反覆調整凸顯能見度不足；Meridian Ag Advisors的Wesley Davis則警告，取消零售商熟悉的獎勵措施，可能使公司進一步流失市占。

CityFibre則要求債權人承擔損失，並協助出資整併。據知情人士及Bloomberg看到的簡報，公司股東在本週稍早會議提出，將約£20億貸款中的一部分減記並換取股權；其餘債務則希望取得以新增借款支付利息的選項。剩餘債務將部分留在營運公司，部分移至控股公司。

股東進一步投入£9億的前提，是與貸款銀行達成協議。相關出資方包括高盛、Antin Infrastructure Partners、Mubadala及Interogo；擬提供的股東貸款將進入控股公司，並與移轉至該公司的債務享有同等順位。因此，除了立即減讓本金與減輕現金付息負擔，債權如何分配於兩個實體之間，也是談判重點。

執行長Simon Holden將Netomnia列為優先收購對象，正考慮年底前重新出價；Community Fibre與Hyperoptic也是選項，潛在交易可同時推進。CityFibre在2025年底約有£38.1億銀行貸款，於2029年6月到期，稅前虧損則由£3.60億擴大至£5.45億。融資成本上升、網路投資變現緩慢，使公司更迫切需要與貸款銀行及收購對象達成協議；若努力失敗，債權人最快可能在明年取得控制權。

知情人士表示，Hain Celestial正考慮最快下月聲請美國破產法第11章保護，尚未作最後決定。公司擬將英國與歐洲業務出售予Aurelius，交易條件要求貸款銀行將12月到期債務至少展延九個月；然而10月12日期限已過，所需信貸協議修改仍未完成。這項原可帶來最多$3.10億償債資金的出售案仍在協商。Hain約有$6.55億無擔保債務，表示仍在轉型計畫下評估策略與財務選項。

香港新世界發展公布換債參與情況：截至10月14日提前交付期限，持有人提交$1.891億，低於$6億上限。換債涵蓋約$9.91億、於2027年1月及6月與2028年到期的債券，換入2032年到期新券。要約開放至10月20日，但額外現金獎勵僅適用提前交付者。這項參與數字讓投資人得以重新衡量既有再融資計畫的涵蓋程度。

銀行也重新檢視先前難以分銷的收購債務。摩根大通考慮縮小Qualtrics收購Press Ganey Forsta的融資，可能各以約$20億高收益債與槓桿貸款組成，並加強貸款人保障。先前$53億融資因市場擔憂AI顛覆軟體業而受阻，使承銷銀行自行提供收購資金。Qualtrics既有2030年到期貸款週三報價約面額每美元84美分；第2季營收$7.18億，前季為$7.20億，調整後EBITDA則由去年同期$2.578億增至$3.32億。銀行計畫以最新第3季業績重新向投資人銷售。

另一宗收購融資的競爭仍熱絡。摩根大通與Jefferies主導Curium收購Lantheus的銀行團，其他貸款人正爭取在明年聯貸前加入。融資包括$42.5億優先擔保B類定期貸款、多幣別循環額度，以及$11.25億以債付息（PIK）融資；知情人士表示，PIK部分已完成配售。收購總值最高達$80億，其中包括與商業里程碑連動的或有付款。

Pizza Hut已為可能的全業務證券化展開初步會議，以支應LongRange Capital的$15億收購。UBS負責協調，下週ABS East會議期間還將繼續洽談。擬議債務將以加盟費等可產生現金的資產作融資基礎，結構與發行仍在研議。另方面，摩根士丹利正為America First Refining位於布朗斯維爾、規模$40億的計畫籌措股權與債務。Reliance是投資人，並已同意採購燃料20年。計畫預計2029年啟動，發起人也正爭取可能的《國防生產法》支持。

歐洲銀行持續測試信用風險移轉需求。UniCredit正洽談對€10億德國住宅房貸提供無資金型保障，另有一筆以約€10億捷克中小企業貸款為標的的交易；KBC則在籌備連結逾€20億企業貸款的重大風險移轉（SRT）。依Crescent Capital，上半年SRT擔保資產中，住宅房貸僅占2%。無資金型結構以支付票息換取保險公司保證，不要求投資人預先出資；歐洲政策制定者評估資本減免時，正檢視這項差異。三宗提案皆仍在與投資人討論。

一筆已完成的小型交易則顯示，保證可協助企業取得融資。Valency取得Green Guarantee Co.的$6,000萬保證，由滙豐安排發債、Legal & General買進。資金將支應象牙海岸一座將腰果廢棄物轉為生質油與能源的設施，屬$1.5億計畫的一部分。發行人境遇雖各不相同，美國高收益債整體利差當天仍小幅收窄；公債殖利率下降支撐債券報酬，LQD上漲0.82%、HYG上漲0.42%，新興市場債券基金EMB上漲0.67%。

## 歐洲衡量市場緊縮與財政可信度

ECB管理委員會成員Primoz Dolenc表示，金融市場條件收緊，可減少官員原本需要透過貨幣政策施加的緊縮程度。經過兩次升息，他認為政策已接近具限制性的界線，但可能尚未跨過。經濟學家預期12月再升息，將存款利率提高至2.75%。Dolenc指出，第二輪通膨效應尚未出現；傳導保護工具是否可用，仍須視需要及資格條件而定。

拉脫維亞的Martins Kazaks也支持審慎掌握時間。他認為近期通膨上行風險大於成長下行風險，但警告經濟活動受創可能非線性加劇。他判斷ECB並未落後情勢，政策方向仍朝緊縮；借款成本進入限制性區間後，取捨將更困難。他也支持在有政策理由時考慮提高最低準備要求，並清楚說明原因。

前荷蘭央行總裁Klaas Knot提出較長期的觀點：地緣政治與供給衝擊反覆發生，可能使ECB更常從高於2%目標的通膨水準向下收斂，因此需要略偏鷹派的立場。他支持目前循序漸進的做法，並表示1月薪資談判尤其重要，因為歐洲許多合約屆時重訂。目前他認為工會要求與第二輪效應仍受控制。他反對以逆轉量化緊縮來因應債市危機，認為重新評估應基於結構性的流動性需求。

法國附買回市場與其公債賣壓形成重要對照。依CME資料，以法國公債作擔保放出現金，相對將現金存入央行的利差，短暫急升後已回到約12個基點，僅略高於三個月均值；交易員表示目前融資並無困難。巴克萊Rohan Khanna認為，這種穩定顯示投資人並未急著籌措現金；TreasurySpring的Glen Stone則區分了短期融資信心與未來多年法國財政風險的疑慮。

Stone指出，若進一步降評使法國跌破擔保品資格門檻，可接受其公債的貸款人將減少，持有成本隨之上升，壓力可能回傳現券市場，但他認為近期出現此情況的可能性不高。Moody’s可能於本月稍晚更新法國評等。Fitch的Federico Barriga-Salazar認為，2027年預算提案是減少赤字的重要嘗試，但警告若未獲通過將帶來不利後果；IMF也敦促及時核准。

前ECB總裁Mario Draghi另指出，出手協助法國仍相當遙遠。與歐債危機時期的低通膨環境不同，目前通膨高且持續上升，物價穩定必須優先。他表示，法國受到過度赤字程序約束，在法律上並未排除ECB工具的使用，但提高了啟動門檻，法國國內對干預的政治爭論也增加行動難度。Kazaks同樣認為，市場失序可能需要回應，但ECB不應替法國解決財政問題。

領導人事的不確定性帶來另一項制度議題。知情官員表示，Christine Lagarde未明確說明是否提前離任，引發部分官員不滿，儘管也有人認為政策可不受影響地推進。西班牙反對黨領袖Alberto Núñez Feijóo週四表態支持Pablo Hernández de Cos接任，讓他在11月29日大選前獲得跨主要政治陣營的支持。De Cos與Knot是領先人選。Isabel Schnabel執行委員席次的提名截止日為10月28日，Philip Lane任期則於5月結束，因此總裁交接時間也牽動更廣泛的人事協商。

英國家庭數據則揭示政策與財政展望的另一種限制。8月GDP意外成長，主要由製造業帶動，面向消費者的服務業卻萎縮。Bloomberg Intelligence調查發現，55%受訪者若無收入，支付帳單的能力撐不過三個月，較一年前增加13個百分點；每十人便有一人近期曾漏繳或延後付款。英國央行數據顯示，8月無擔保借款創紀錄增加£25億，信用卡違約連續第六季上升，為2009年以來最長紀錄。副總裁Sarah Breeden表示，消費者正承受生活成本壓力。能源與房貸成本偏高，影響支出與稅基，也使財政大臣John Healey的10月28日預算更難安排。

## 亞洲政策與主權融資走向分歧

MUFG銀行大幅降低利率曝險後，開始試探性買進日本公債。全球市場主管Atsushi Yamashita表示，已在10年期殖利率約3.1%時開始少量買進，將逐步重建部位。該行日本公債投資組合的存續期間，由去年9月3.1年降至今年6月1.2年。東京週四10年期殖利率下降8.5個基點至2.91%，三井住友DS資產管理的Shinji Kunibe認為，國內大型買家提供了心理支撐。

Yamashita的基本情境是殖利率在3.2%附近觸頂；但若通膨超過日本央行緊縮步伐，或財政政策損及信心，仍可能升至3%區間中高段。他預期日本央行12月再升息，之後約每三個月一次，終端利率約2%；若通膨需要，終點可能更高。他排除為購買日本公債而出售海外資產，並表示有吸引力的殖利率也可能帶來增加外國債券投資的空間。

日本央行審議委員Junko Koeda在熊本演講時，進一步表達對緊縮的支持。她表示，物價上行風險與仍寬鬆的金融條件，意味政策不宜過度謹慎；她估計中性利率明顯高於1%，因此目前1.25%的政策利率仍有調升空間，但未指定步調，也未暗示10月即將升息。週四隔夜交換價格反映本月升息機率約5%，12月前則為87%。財務大臣片山皋月另警告，必要時日本可再次干預匯市，並表示7月與美國共同干預的立場仍維持不變。

紐西蘭央行首席經濟學家Paul Conway表示，10月28日仍可能維持利率或升息25個基點；第3季兩度升息至2.75%後，央行刻意保留兩種選擇。市場反映10月升息機率略高於60%，並已完全反映12月升至3%。Conway認為，政策最可能的方向仍向上；高油價與匯率走弱，使央行原先預期通膨由第2季4.1%降至年底3.9%的預測面臨上行風險。央行仍預期明年通膨回到1%至3%目標區間。

澳洲就業數據則使預期往相反方向走。失業率上升、就業人數減少，促使投資人降低澳洲央行升息押注，澳元一度下跌1.1%至$0.6894，為7月初以來最低。CIBC的Maximillian Lin表示，數據支持11月維持利率，但就業數字波動大，12月仍可能升息。馬來西亞央行總裁Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour則表示，9月刪除政策「適當」的措辭，是為了增加因應通膨的空間；即使交換市場反映六個月內升息機率約76%，他仍認為2.75%利率符合展望。他以電子業訂單能見度由五個月前約六個月延長至12至18個月，說明需求仍在持續。

印度護匯使債市面臨更棘手的盤算。Ujjivan Small Finance Bank與IDFC First Bank分析師預期，10年期殖利率最快本月便可能由週三7.4%升至7.5%。Ujjivan的Rajeev Pawar表示，交易員認為12月升息50個基點的可能性增加；PGIM India的Puneet Pal則預期，若印度央行護匯後仍需提高利率，殖利率未來一個月可能升至7.60%。

IDFC First Bank經濟學家Gaura Sen Gupta著重美元拋售對流動性的影響：銀行體系的盧比被收回，可用於買進公債的資金減少。她將短期殖利率預期區間調整為7.20%至7.50%，先前約為7.25%，並認為相較升息，市場對流動性收緊的準備較不足。盧比本週已升值1.6%至每美元約95盧比。烏干達先令也延續升息後反彈，倫敦週四下午升值0.8%至每美元4,043。Alpha Capital的Stephen Kaboyo與Absa的Richard Nsubuga將部分升勢歸因於央行賣出美元，但央行尚未證實。

南韓海外借款人除殖利率上升外，也面臨監管問題。知情人士表示，Lotte Rental延後首次美元發債，部分因政府非正式反對加入未持有本地證券牌照的KGI Asia，程序拖延至市況惡化。Lotte則表示，延後主要因美債殖利率上升，時程反映公司自行就殖利率作出的決定。南韓今年外幣發債規模已增加32%至$670億，當局正考慮限制無本地牌照的海外安排機構。

阿根廷境內美元債殖利率已上升逾500個基點至12%以上，使發債暫停期延長至兩個月。新定價阻礙今年原計畫再籌近$10億，而2027年10月大選前後到期債券的殖利率差，也擴大至近500個基點。Caputo仍預期明年可在境內發債，並將中國換匯協議列為備案。該協議可動用部分向央行提供人民幣，條款未完全公開，因此將資金用於財政部還債的途徑，與發行美元債不同。

智利退休基金的新報導揭露，業者主管曾私下要求監管機關限制自身日益增加的海外利率衍生品曝險，因為單方面收斂部位可能在競爭中落後。監管首長Joaquín Cortez表示，評斷經理人的投資決定並非其職責，並指出監管機關早在2024年便警告衍生品風險，2025年1月也要求修改政策。產業協會反對將相關部位稱為押注，表示衍生品是管理長期現金流的常規工具。這些互有分歧的說法，使已揭露損失事件的責任問題，在11月初合規期限前更受關注。

中國的美元資產與國內失衡則分別受到檢視。DoubleLine的Vitaliy Liberman及前美國財政部官員Brad Setser等投資人與專家懷疑，加拿大持有的近$6,000億美國公債與機構證券中，一部分其實是中國透過海外保管機構持有的資產。加拿大總持有額五年內增至四倍以上，其中機構抵押貸款證券由2021年中約$210億增至約$1,620億。Bloomberg未發現這些增幅與中國有關的直接證據；Vanda Research的Alex Etra指出，加拿大避險基金相對價值交易可能解釋部分累積，對完全歸因於中國的說法提出不同看法。

IMF的Krishna Srinivasan認為，人民幣實質匯率低估反映內需疲弱與刺激不足。IMF在2026年評估的低估幅度為17.3%至25.3%，中點21.3%。中國央行則主張，這項實質匯率評估並非對名目匯率的判斷，支持的是國內再平衡，而非刻意讓人民幣對個別貨幣升值。Gavekal的Andrew Batson與Xiaoxi Zhang在週三報告另提出企業融資觀察：8月應收帳款推算的平均收款時間創紀錄達72天。他們認為，長期疲弱的經濟使企業財務惡化、欠款加劇，但也說明該指標不能直接與政府對大型企業的60天付款標準比較。

## 後續市場觀察重點

聯準會主席Kevin Warsh預定10月16日03:30 UTC在曼谷發表談話，換算紐約時間為週四晚間11:30，已在美國債市收盤之後。這是10月27至28日會議前、週六進入緘默期之前，最後一個主要政策溝通機會。當前焦點在於強勁的生產者物價與支出，是否會改變Daly表達的耐心，以及殖利率下降與AI投資疑慮如何改變金融緊縮的平衡。9月PCE在政策決議後才公布，官員必須在完整數據出爐前評估其可能組成。

週五紐約時間上午8:30公布9月進出口物價，將補足通膨圖像。市場預期進口與出口物價分別月增0.8%及1%，前值為0.7%與0.6%。上午9:15公布工業生產，預期由前月持平轉為增加0.4%；製造業生產預期由減少0.3%轉為增加0.3%，產能利用率則預期由76.3%升至76.5%。全國產出數據將可與10月紐約、費城製造業調查的明顯分歧相互對照。

財政部週五向交易商發出的問卷，是11月再融資公告前，下一項有關債務管理選項的溝通。週四已實際買回$60億長天期公債，問卷則可能透露官員是否考慮調整未來發債。週五預期公布的9月預算收支為赤字$290億，前值赤字$1,670億；8月TIC長期資本流動預期淨流入$752億，前值淨流出$279億，將分別補充財政及跨境需求資訊。海外保管歸屬的爭論，也使外國持有部位的組成與歸屬，和總資金流同樣值得關注。

新世界10月20日換債截止，將揭示$1.891億提前交付之外的最終參與規模。CityFibre取得股東融資仍以貸款銀行同意為條件，Hain持續中的資產出售談判則須解決債務到期條件。Qualtrics擬重返聯貸市場，將測試在軟體業曝險仍受質疑之際，較小融資與較強保障能否吸引貸款人。FMC的10月29日業績與10月30日展望，將讓債權人更完整掌握定價調整與融資需求。

紐西蘭央行10月28日決議與日本央行10月30日會議即將登場，官員支持進一步緊縮，但仍保留時機上的彈性。法國預算能否通過，以及Moody’s可能更新評等，則更直接考驗主權信用信心，目前附買回融資仍穩定。週四晚間報導指出，歐盟正準備擴大權限，可能據此限制進入單一市場，並研議對化學品與機械實施進口配額。這些擬議措施將貿易爭端從既有的油電混合車進口上限擴及其他領域；各國央行衡量緊縮幅度之際，供給與價格又增添一項未定因素。

紐西蘭10月28日及日本央行10月30日決策將至，官員支持進一步緊縮，但仍保留時機選擇。法國預算能否通過、Moody’s是否更新評等，則是更直接的主權信心考驗，目前附買回融資仍穩定。週四晚間報導指出，歐盟正準備擴大權限，可能關閉單一市場准入，並研究對化學品與機械實施進口配額。這些擬議貿易措施使爭端超出既有油電混合車上限；央行決定緊縮幅度時，又多了一項尚未定案的供給與價格問題。

overall_summary.session_narrative:
亞洲科技股隔夜崩跌，加深市場對AI融資及其投資、成長影響的擔憂，帶動美債大漲。10年期殖利率下降12.74個基點至5.058%，2年期下降5.93個基點至4.7382%，使2年與10年期利差收窄6.81個基點至31.98個基點。漲勢主要來自實質殖利率下降：10年期實質殖利率下降9.65個基點至2.7283%，損益兩平通膨率下降3.09個基點至2.3297%。

9月PPI月增1.3%、零售銷售增加0.8%，均高於預期，僅短暫打斷美債漲勢；經濟學家仍依相關PPI分項下修9月PCE預測。Mary Daly支持進一步緊縮，但無須立即行動；交換市場仍預期年底前再升息。市政債同步上漲，紐約時間下午4時，指標10年期殖利率下降16個基點至3.74%。

標普500由跌轉漲，Nvidia的黃仁勳力挺CoreWeave財務狀況後，後者股價收漲5.9%。不過，CoreWeave的5年期違約保障成本盤中仍創1,194.5個基點新高，公司債務超過$400億，自由現金流缺口也日益擴大。FMC調整定價後，2031年到期債券殖利率約10.5%；CityFibre爭取債權人讓步，Hain則考慮聲請破產法第11章保護。美國高收益債整體利差小幅收窄，更凸顯公債反彈與個別借款人再融資能力的差異。
overall_summary.summary: AI投資與成長疑慮壓過強勁的生產者物價及零售銷售，10年期美債殖利率下降12.74個基點，主要來自實質殖利率下滑。CoreWeave違約保障成本盤中創新高，顯示股市反彈後信用壓力仍未消退。

section_summaries.summary: 強勁的美國通膨與支出數據，以及股市回穩，都未削弱中長天期美債需求。亞洲科技股賣壓背後的AI融資疑慮，也引發投資與成長可能受創的擔憂。市政債上漲、美國高收益債整體利差小幅收窄，但CoreWeave及科技業以外的借款人仍承受嚴重信用壓力。

section_summaries.market_read: 當日漲勢降低實質借款成本，但10年期實質殖利率本月仍上升12.13個基點。

section_summaries.market_read: 供應商與大型投資人對AI擴張仍有財務曝險，債權人則重新評估需要多少營收才能支撐相關債務。
section_summaries.section_title: CoreWeave股價反彈，信用壓力未退
section_summaries.summary: 黃仁勳力挺財務狀況後，CoreWeave股價上漲5.9%，但5年期違約保障成本盤中仍創1,194.5個基點新高。逾$400億債務與日益擴大的自由現金流缺口，使償債能力持續受關注；公司主張已簽約的積壓訂單足以支應義務。Stack尋求$60億資料中心貸款，台積電與Anthropic較強的營收表現則顯示，融資焦慮與可觀AI需求並存。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied sharply on October 15 as an overnight collapse in Asian technology shares intensified concern about the financing of artificial intelligence and drew investors into government debt. The 10-year yield fell 12.74 basis points to 5.058%, while the two-year declined a smaller 5.93 basis points to 4.7382%. Longer maturities led the advance even after September producer prices and retail sales exceeded expectations, leaving the market weighing prospective damage to investment and growth against continuing pressure for Federal Reserve tightening.

The flight into duration survived a substantial recovery in U.S. equities. The S&P 500 finished higher, and Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang helped CoreWeave shares reverse their initial losses. Credit investors remained less reassured: CoreWeave’s five-year default-protection cost reached a record intraday level, and individual borrowers outside technology suffered severe repricing. Municipal bonds joined the government rally, while broad U.S. high-yield spreads ended modestly tighter. The session combined a powerful recovery in interest-rate exposure with persistent distinctions over which companies could service, refinance or expand their debt.

## Treasuries Rally Through Stronger Prices and Spending

Much of the Treasury advance occurred before U.S. trading began. South Korea’s Kospi fell nearly 8%, taking its decline from the September high to about 21%, as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each lost more than 9%. Trading was halted for 20 minutes during the selloff. Foreign investors sold $2.7 billion of Korean equities Thursday, bringing their October selling above $10 billion. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped nearly 5%, and Taiwan’s Taiex fell 3.4% as overseas investors sold a record NT$302.6 billion, or $9.3 billion, of shares.

Those moves carried the financing anxiety surrounding AI into economies heavily exposed to semiconductor investment. Treasury yields fell by as much as 12-15 basis points across maturities during the day. Reports of larger-than-expected U.S. producer-price and retail-sales increases interrupted the advance only briefly. Wells Fargo strategist Angelo Manolatos attributed the price action to risk aversion and AI concerns, while Deutsche Bank’s Steven Zeng said investors were looking beyond strong current data toward possible economic stress if the sector’s problems deepened.

The closing curve showed the greater demand for intermediate and long debt. Five-year yields fell 10.94 basis points to 4.8775%, and the 30-year declined 11.75 basis points to 5.4056%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 6.81 basis points to 31.98, while 2s30s contracted 5.82 to 66.74. Over the week, 10-year yields were down 16.88 basis points and 30-year yields down 19.45, compared with a decline of only 1.95 basis points at two years. Policy expectations continued to constrain the shortest coupon maturity even as demand for duration strengthened.

Inflation-linked debt supplied a clearer decomposition of the rally. The 10-year real yield fell 9.65 basis points to 2.7283%, accounting for most of the nominal yield decline, while 10-year breakeven inflation fell 3.09 basis points to 2.3297%. Over the month, nominal 10-year yields were still 7 basis points higher: real yields had risen 12.13 basis points, partly offset by a 5.13-basis-point fall in inflation compensation. Thursday brought relief from elevated real borrowing costs without erasing their monthly increase.

September’s producer-price report nevertheless gave the Fed another strong inflation reading. Headline PPI rose 1.3% month on month against a 0.5% consensus and an upwardly revised 0.5% previous increase. Annual producer inflation accelerated to 6.3% from a revised 5.6%, exceeding the expected 5.3%. Core PPI increased 0.7% on the month, compared with 0.3% expected and 0.2% previously; its annual rate reached 5%, versus a 4.4% consensus and a revised 4.8% prior reading.

The measure excluding food, energy and trade services increased 0.5% month on month after 0.3%, with annual growth at 5% after a revised 4.8%. The breadth of those increases kept the report from being solely an energy story. Yet Bloomberg’s Treasury account said the components economists use to estimate the Fed’s preferred consumer-inflation measure broadly led them to lower their estimates of September PCE inflation. That release is scheduled for the day after the October 28 policy decision, making the distinction between the producer-price headline and its implications for consumer inflation particularly consequential.

Retail sales increased 0.8% in September, comfortably above the 0.3% consensus, after a revised 1.3% increase. Gasoline spending contributed to the strength. Annex Wealth Management’s Brian Jacobsen argued that expensive fuel was crowding out purchases elsewhere, while eToro’s Bret Kenwell stressed that nominal sales were not adjusted for inflation. Wells Fargo Investment Institute’s Gary Schlossberg expects consumer spending to moderate, with direct and indirect support from AI investment limiting the slowdown. The same investment cycle unsettling markets therefore remained an important support in that economic assessment.

Labor-market figures offered little evidence of an abrupt deterioration. Initial unemployment claims were 199,000 for the week ended October 10, against 200,000 expected and a revised 198,000 previously. Continuing claims fell to 1.710 million for the week ended October 3 from a revised 1.714 million, matching consensus. The Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow estimate for Q3 remained 3.6%.

The regional manufacturing surveys were more divided. The Empire State index jumped to 25.50 in October from 7.60, far above the 10.3 consensus. Philadelphia’s headline manufacturing index fell to 20.9 from 37.8 and missed the expected 28.4. Its new-orders index dropped to 4.3 from 29.2, employment eased to 9.1 from 11.8, and prices paid fell to 43.20 from 48.60. Forward business conditions declined to 33.0 from 52.9, while capital-expenditure intentions slipped to 34.90 from 37.10. Expansion persisted, but Philadelphia’s order and outlook measures presented a distinctly softer picture than New York’s acceleration.

August business inventories increased 0.4%, matching consensus after a revised 0.9% rise. Retail inventories excluding autos were flat, versus a 0.1% increase expected and 0.8% previously. Alongside the divergent factory surveys, those figures complicated any reading of stronger nominal consumption as uniformly stronger demand across the economy.

San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly supplied a separate policy signal in a Wednesday Reuters interview reported in the current news window. She judged further rate increases more likely than not but saw no need to act immediately, leaving their timing under deliberation. Thursday’s swap pricing still anticipated another increase by year-end, including roughly a 30% probability of an October move, according to Bloomberg’s Treasury account. Expectations for the subsequent sequence moderated, with fewer than three additional quarter-point increases fully priced. Daly’s preference preserved a distinction between supporting more restraint and supporting another move this month.

The rally extended to municipal debt. Benchmark 10-year muni yields fell 16 basis points to 3.74% at 4 p.m. New York, their biggest one-day decline since April 2025, while 30-year yields dropped 15 basis points to 4.97%. CIBC Private Wealth Management’s Chris Lanouette linked the long-end support to the retreat from equities; DWS’s Chad Farrington also cited continuing positive ETF flows. Treasury’s expanded buyback program separately purchased its maximum $6 billion in the 10- to 20-year sector Thursday.

By the U.S. equity close, the S&P 500 had recovered to a 0.33% gain, while the Nasdaq 100 was down just 0.05%. Semiconductor shares still lost 0.88%, leaving the sector 8.26% lower over the week. The Dollar Index fell 0.53% to 102.004, and gold futures rose 1.82% to $4,182.80 an ounce. Energy supplied mixed relief: Brent slipped 0.41% to $105.62 a barrel, but WTI rose 2.60% to $97.56. EIA reported an 8.557 million-barrel crude-stock draw, much larger than the expected 0.3 million draw, alongside a 3.518 million-barrel gasoline build against an expected 0.5 million decline. Fuel balances remained uneven as bonds recovered.

## CoreWeave’s Credit Stress Outlasts Its Equity Rebound

CoreWeave’s credit insurance became more expensive Thursday even as an intervention from its most important supplier helped restore confidence in its shares. Five-year protection rose by as much as 74.5 basis points to 1,194.5 basis points, an intraday record, according to ICE Data Services. At that point, swaps implied a probability above 60% of default over five years. That market-implied measure marked a further deterioration from the above-50% reading reported a day earlier.

Cash bonds also showed renewed pressure, though individual issues diverged. At 11 a.m. New York, the company’s 9% notes due in 2031 had fallen about 2.5 cents to 80.75 cents on the dollar, yielding 15.3%. Its 9.25% notes due in 2030 declined roughly 0.75 cents to about 86, yielding 14.3%. The 9.75% 2031 notes edged up 0.125 cents to 80.625. The distinction between those securities matters in a company whose borrowing spans different structures and coupons, rather than a single uniform financing cost.

Huang defended CoreWeave in Stockholm, saying its financial strength was improving and its cost of capital decreasing. Nvidia is both a major supplier and CoreWeave’s second-largest shareholder, with about a 10% stake. CoreWeave shares erased earlier losses and closed 5.9% higher at $69.69. Huang said Nvidia did not need to backstop the company. His assessment contrasted with the distressed cash-bond yields and record protection costs investors were observing that day.

The company’s financing requirement explains the sensitivity to that disagreement. Wall Street estimates put year-end sales at $12.9 billion, with revenue more than doubling again next year, against more than $40 billion of debt and substantial repayments over the next five years. Free cash flow has become increasingly negative, and analysts expect losses above $2.5 billion this year. CoreWeave maintains that its contracted backlog supports repayment of secured and unsecured obligations without customer renewals or re-leasing collateral. The current dispute concerns the value and funding of rapid expansion against those obligations, with suppliers financially invested in its success.

New financing plans elsewhere showed that the buildout was continuing. Blue Owl-owned Stack Infrastructure mandated arrangers, underwriters and bookrunners this week for a proposed five-year A$8.6 billion, or $6 billion, loan to finance a Melbourne data-center project, a person familiar with the matter said. The request could become one of the region’s largest sector financings. Goldman Sachs estimated in a September report that global AI-related debt issuance had reached about $578 billion this year, with hyperscalers accounting for 40%.

Operating evidence remained stronger than the market reaction alone suggested. TSMC delivered a better-than-expected revenue outlook, although its quarterly gross margin was slightly below analysts’ estimates. Anthropic told prospective investors Q3 revenue reached $16.8 billion and that it achieved adjusted profitability. A separate account reported positive free cash flow and an 85% gross margin. The company is preparing to begin formal IPO marketing as soon as November 9 for a possible year-end debut. Investors’ concern over a slowing growth pace accompanied substantial actual revenue, rather than an absence of demand.

The exposure also extends well beyond cloud operators. Blackstone president Jon Gray described AI investment as central to the firm, whose data-center holdings have reached $200 billion. Its involvement includes a cloud venture with Google, stakes in OpenAI, loans secured against Broadcom and Nvidia chips, and investment in power plants and cooling equipment. A Gartner analysis cited in late-Thursday coverage estimated that $3.5 trillion of AI infrastructure spending could face impairment as soon as 2030 if investment outpaced the revenue needed to justify it. That is a prospective assessment of asset economics, alongside continued capital commitments by major investors.

Asia’s dependence on that spending remained a material economic distinction. The IMF raised its 2026 regional growth forecast to 4.8%, partly because of AI investment, while projecting a slowdown to 4.4% next year. It warned that a correction in investment or valuations would hit economies at the center of the technology supply chain particularly hard. Elsewhere in electronics, IDC reported a record 22% drop in global smartphone shipments last quarter as memory costs rose roughly 350% over a year. The research firm does not expect shipments to resume growth until at least 2028. Strong demand for computing inputs was imposing costs on other users even before any contraction in infrastructure spending.

## Borrowers Seek New Terms as Credit Outcomes Diverge

FMC supplied one of the day’s sharpest credit moves outside AI. Its investment-grade bonds due in 2031 traded at a yield of about 10.5% after the crop-chemical producer announced a major pricing overhaul. Weak demand, expensive inventories held by distributors and competition from generics have impeded replenishment orders. The company plans to narrow the difference between gross and net U.S. prices, moving away from a model of high initial prices and large rebates, and to lower prices in Brazil, Argentina and Canada.

FMC estimates a Q3 impact of $625 million-$675 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $510 million-$565 million. It expects compliance with its covenants at September 30 but intends to discuss further modifications with lenders over the next year to gain flexibility for the overhaul. The shares fell as much as 40%. Barclays analysts led by Benjamin Theurer said repeated changes to operations and guidance underscored poor visibility, while Meridian Ag Advisors’ Wesley Davis warned that removing familiar retailer incentives could cost further market share.

CityFibre is asking creditors to absorb losses and help finance consolidation. At a meeting earlier this week, its owners proposed a partial writedown of an approximately £2 billion loan in exchange for equity, according to people familiar with the talks and a presentation seen by Bloomberg. The company also wants the option to pay interest on the remaining debt with additional borrowing. Part would remain at the operating company and part would move to the holding company.

An agreement with lenders is a condition for a further £900 million from stakeholders including Goldman Sachs, Antin Infrastructure Partners, Mubadala and Interogo. Their proposed shareholder loan would enter at the holding company and rank equally with the debt transferred there. That placement makes the allocation of claims between the two entities central to the negotiation, alongside the immediate principal concession and relief from cash interest.

Chief executive Simon Holden identified Netomnia as the preferred acquisition target and is considering a renewed offer before year-end. Community Fibre and Hyperoptic are other possibilities, and the potential transactions are not mutually exclusive. CityFibre had about £3.81 billion of bank loans at end-2025, due in June 2029, and its pretax loss widened to £545 million from £360 million. Rising funding costs and slow monetization of network investment have increased pressure to reach agreements with lenders and acquisition targets; creditors could take control as soon as next year if those efforts fail.

Hain Celestial is weighing Chapter 11 protection as soon as next month, people familiar with the discussions said, with no final decision. A proposed sale of its UK and European businesses to Aurelius had required lenders to extend December debt maturities by at least nine months. The October 12 deadline passed without the required credit-agreement changes. The sale, which could have generated as much as $310 million for debt repayment, remains under negotiation. Hain has about $655 million of unsecured debt and says it continues to evaluate strategic and financial alternatives as part of its turnaround.

In Hong Kong, New World Development disclosed a concrete measure of participation in its debt exchange. Holders tendered $189.1 million by the October 14 early deadline, below the $600 million cap. The offer covers approximately $991 million of notes due in January and June 2027 and in 2028, exchanging them for 2032 maturities. It remains open until October 20, but the additional cash incentives applied only to early tenders. The participation figure gives investors a fresh indication of the reach of a refinancing effort already under way.

Banks are also revisiting debt they previously struggled to distribute. JPMorgan is considering a smaller financing for Qualtrics’ acquisition of Press Ganey Forsta, potentially split into roughly $2 billion each of high-yield bonds and leveraged loans. The package could carry stronger lender protections. A prior $5.3 billion attempt stalled amid concern over AI disruption to software businesses, leaving the underwriting banks funding the acquisition. Qualtrics’ existing 2030 loan was quoted around 84 cents Wednesday, while its Q2 revenue was $718 million against $720 million in the preceding period. Adjusted EBITDA increased to $332 million from $257.8 million a year earlier. The banks plan to use fresh Q3 earnings in a renewed sales effort.

Competition for another acquisition financing remained active. JPMorgan and Jefferies are leading the bank group for Curium’s Lantheus purchase, with other lenders seeking to join ahead of syndication next year. The package includes a $4.25 billion senior secured term loan B, a multicurrency revolver and a $1.125 billion payment-in-kind facility. The PIK has already been placed, people familiar with the matter said. That financing supports an acquisition worth up to $8 billion, including contingent payments linked to commercial milestones.

Pizza Hut has begun preliminary meetings for a possible whole-business securitization to finance its $1.5 billion buyout by LongRange Capital. UBS is coordinating discussions, with further meetings planned at next week’s ABS East conference. The proposed debt would borrow against cash-generating assets including franchise fees; structure and issuance remain under consideration. Separately, Morgan Stanley is raising equity and debt for America First Refining’s $4 billion Brownsville project. Reliance is an investor and has agreed to buy fuel for 20 years. The project expects to start in 2029, while its sponsor is also seeking potential Defense Production Act support.

European banks continued testing demand for credit-risk transfers. UniCredit is discussing unfunded protection on €1 billion of German residential mortgages and a separate transaction referencing about €1 billion of Czech small- and medium-sized-company loans. KBC is working on an SRT tied to more than €2 billion of corporate loans. Residential mortgages accounted for just 2% of SRT collateral in the first half, according to Crescent Capital. Unfunded structures exchange an insurer’s guarantee for a coupon rather than requiring upfront investor cash, a distinction European policymakers are examining when assessing capital relief. All three proposals remain in investor discussions.

A smaller completed transaction illustrated the role of guarantees in expanding funding access. Valency obtained a $60 million Green Guarantee Co. guarantee for an HSBC-arranged bond acquired by Legal & General. Proceeds support an Ivory Coast facility converting cashew waste into bio-oils and energy, part of a $150 million plan. Against these varied issuer outcomes, U.S. high-yield spreads finished modestly tighter; LQD returned 0.82%, HYG 0.42% and emerging-market debt fund EMB 0.67% for the day as falling government yields supported bond returns.

## Europe Weighs Market Restraint and Fiscal Credibility

ECB Governing Council member Primoz Dolenc said financial-market tightening could reduce the amount of monetary restraint officials otherwise needed to deliver. Following two increases, he judged policy close to the restrictive boundary, though probably not yet across it. Economists anticipate another move in December to a 2.75% deposit rate. Dolenc said second-round effects were not yet visible, while keeping the availability of the Transmission Protection Instrument conditional on need and eligibility.

Latvia’s Martins Kazaks independently supported taking time. He judged near-term inflation risks larger than downside growth risks but warned that damage to activity could become nonlinear. In his assessment the ECB was not behind the curve, even though the direction of policy remained toward tightening. As borrowing costs move into restrictive territory, he expects the tradeoffs to become harder. He also supported considering higher minimum reserve requirements if there were a policy case, with clear communication of the rationale.

Former Dutch central-bank chief Klaas Knot offered a longer-horizon assessment. Repeated geopolitical and supply disruptions could leave the ECB approaching its 2% inflation target from above more often, requiring a mildly hawkish stance. He supported its current measured approach and said wage negotiations in January would be particularly important because many European contracts reset then. So far, he regarded union demands and second-round effects as contained. He opposed using a reversal of quantitative tightening as a crisis response to bond-market conditions, arguing that any reassessment should instead reflect structural liquidity needs.

France’s repo market supplied a material counterpoint to its sovereign selloff. After a brief spike, the cost of lending cash against French government collateral relative to depositing it at a central bank settled around 12 basis points, only slightly above its three-month average, according to CME data. Traders reported no current difficulty financing the bonds. Barclays’ Rohan Khanna said that stability suggested investors were not scrambling for cash, while TreasurySpring’s Glen Stone distinguished short-term financing confidence from concern about French fiscal risk over years.

Stone identified a specific potential transmission channel if further downgrades pushed France below collateral thresholds: fewer lenders could accept the bonds, increasing the cost of holding them and feeding pressure back into the cash market. He regards that outcome as unlikely immediately. Moody’s may update France’s rating later this month. Fitch’s Federico Barriga-Salazar called the 2027 budget proposal a meaningful attempt to reduce the deficit but warned of adverse consequences if it failed to pass; the IMF urged timely approval.

Former ECB president Mario Draghi separately argued that intervention to help France remained a distant prospect. High and rising inflation made price stability the first priority, unlike the low-inflation setting of the euro crisis. France’s Excessive Deficit Procedure did not legally exclude use of ECB instruments, he said, but raised the bar, while domestic political debate over intervention made action more difficult. Kazaks likewise said disorderly markets could require a response but that the ECB should not solve France’s fiscal problems.

Leadership uncertainty added another institutional issue. Officials familiar with discussions described frustration over Christine Lagarde’s lack of clarity on a possible early departure, although some believed policy could proceed unaffected. Spain’s opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo endorsed Pablo Hernández de Cos as her successor Thursday, extending support across the country’s main political divide ahead of the November 29 election. De Cos and Knot are leading contenders. Nominations for Isabel Schnabel’s Executive Board seat are due October 28, with Philip Lane’s term ending in May, making the timing of the presidency relevant to wider negotiations.

British household data exposed a different constraint on the policy and fiscal outlook. August GDP unexpectedly grew, largely because of manufacturing, while consumer-facing services contracted. A Bloomberg Intelligence survey found 55% of respondents could not cover bills for more than three months without income, 13 percentage points more than a year earlier; one in ten had recently missed or delayed a payment. BOE figures showed a record £2.5 billion increase in unsecured borrowing in August and credit-card defaults rising for a sixth consecutive quarter, the longest run since 2009. Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden said consumers were suffering from living-cost pressures. Those strains complicate Chancellor John Healey’s October 28 budget as expensive energy and mortgages bear on spending and the tax base.

## Asian Policy and Sovereign Funding Take Different Paths

MUFG Bank disclosed tentative purchases of Japanese government bonds after a large reduction in interest-rate exposure. Global markets chief Atsushi Yamashita said the bank began exploratory buying of 10-year JGBs around 3.1% and would rebuild gradually. Its JGB portfolio duration had fallen to 1.2 years in June from 3.1 years the previous September. Ten-year yields dropped 8.5 basis points to 2.91% Thursday in Tokyo, with Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management’s Shinji Kunibe citing psychological support from large domestic buyers.

Yamashita’s base case puts the yield peak near 3.2%, but he sees a risk of the mid-to-high 3% range if inflation outpaces BOJ tightening or fiscal policy undermines confidence. He expects the next BOJ increase in December and subsequent moves roughly every three months toward a terminal rate around 2%, potentially higher if inflation warrants it. He ruled out selling foreign assets to finance the domestic purchases and said attractive yields could also create scope to increase foreign-bond investment.

BOJ board member Junko Koeda reinforced support for further tightening in a Kumamoto speech. Upside price risks and still-accommodative financial conditions argued against excessive caution, she said. Her estimate of neutral was considerably above 1%, leaving room for increases from the current 1.25% rate, although she specified no pace and did not signal an imminent October move. Thursday’s overnight swaps implied about a 5% probability of an increase this month and 87% by December. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama separately warned that Japan could act again in currency markets if necessary and said the July joint-intervention stance with Washington remained intact.

New Zealand chief economist Paul Conway said the October 28 decision remained open between holding and raising the cash rate by 25 basis points. After two Q3 increases to 2.75%, the RBNZ deliberately preserved that choice. Markets assigned a little more than 60% probability to an October increase and fully priced a move to 3% in December. Conway said the direction was most likely upward, with expensive oil and a weaker currency creating upside risk to the bank’s forecast that inflation would ease to 3.9% at year-end from 4.1% in Q2. The bank still expects inflation inside its 1%-3% band next year.

Australia’s labor release pushed expectations in the other direction. Higher unemployment and job losses prompted investors to reduce RBA hike bets, taking the Australian dollar as much as 1.1% lower to $0.6894, its weakest since early July. CIBC’s Maximillian Lin said the data supported a November hold but left a December increase possible given volatile employment figures. Malaysia’s Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour, meanwhile, said dropping the description of policy as appropriate in September gave his central bank more room to respond to inflation. The 2.75% rate remained consistent with the outlook, he said, despite swaps implying about a 76% probability of an increase over six months. He cited electronics order books extending to 12-18 months from around six months five months earlier as evidence of continuing demand.

India’s currency defense was producing more difficult bond-market calculations. Ujjivan Small Finance Bank and IDFC First Bank analysts see the 10-year yield reaching 7.5% as soon as this month, against 7.4% Wednesday. Ujjivan’s Rajeev Pawar said traders saw a greater chance of a 50-basis-point December increase. PGIM India’s Puneet Pal expects the yield could reach 7.60% over the next month if the RBI needs higher rates after its currency measures.

IDFC First Bank economist Gaura Sen Gupta emphasized the liquidity effect of dollar sales, which remove rupees from banks and reduce cash available for government debt. She now sees a near-term 7.20%-7.50% yield range, versus an earlier forecast around 7.25%, arguing that expected rate hikes were better anticipated than tighter liquidity. The rupee had gained 1.6% this week to around 95 per dollar. Uganda also extended its post-hike currency recovery, gaining 0.8% to 4,043 per dollar Thursday afternoon in London. Alpha Capital’s Stephen Kaboyo and Absa’s Richard Nsubuga attributed part of the move to central-bank dollar selling, which the bank had not confirmed.

Korea’s offshore borrowers faced a regulatory complication as well as higher yields. People familiar with Lotte Rental’s delayed debut dollar issue said informal government resistance to adding KGI Asia, which lacks a domestic securities license, prolonged the process until market conditions deteriorated. Lotte said rising Treasury yields were the principal reason for postponement and that the schedule reflected its own decisions on yields. Authorities are considering restrictions on offshore arrangers without local licenses in a market where Korean foreign-currency issuance has grown 32% this year to $67 billion.

Argentina’s local dollar-bond yields have risen more than 500 basis points to above 12%, extending its issuance pause to two months. The new pricing shows the obstacle to raising almost another $1 billion planned for this year, while the yield difference between bonds maturing before and after the October 2027 election has widened to nearly 500 basis points. Caputo still expects local issuance next year and has identified the China swap as a contingency. Its usable portion provides yuan to the central bank, with terms not fully public, so its route into Treasury debt payments differs from a dollar bond sale.

Fresh reporting on Chile’s pension funds disclosed that executives had privately asked regulators to impose restrictions on their own growing foreign-rate derivatives exposures because unilateral restraint risked losing ground to competitors. Regulator Joaquín Cortez said assessing managers’ investment decisions was not his role and said the watchdog had warned about derivatives risk in 2024 and demanded policy changes in January 2025. The industry association disputed describing the positions as bets, calling derivatives a standard long-term cash-flow tool. Those competing accounts sharpen accountability for an already-disclosed loss episode ahead of the early-November compliance deadline.

China’s dollar assets and domestic imbalances drew separate scrutiny. Investors including DoubleLine’s Vitaliy Liberman and former Treasury official Brad Setser suspect that some of Canada’s nearly $600 billion in Treasuries and agency securities represents Chinese assets held through foreign custodians. The Canadian total has more than quadrupled in five years; its agency mortgage holdings rose from about $21 billion in mid-2021 to roughly $162 billion. Bloomberg found no direct evidence tying those increases to China. Vanda Research’s Alex Etra said Canadian hedge-fund relative-value trades could explain part of the accumulation, challenging an exclusively Chinese explanation.

The IMF’s Krishna Srinivasan argued that the yuan’s real undervaluation reflected weak domestic demand and insufficient stimulus. The fund’s 2026 assessment estimated undervaluation at 17.3%-25.3%, with a 21.3% midpoint. China’s central bank has argued that this real-rate assessment is not a judgment on the nominal exchange rate and supports domestic rebalancing rather than engineered appreciation against individual currencies. Gavekal’s Andrew Batson and Xiaoxi Zhang added a corporate financing observation in a Wednesday note: the average time implied for collecting receivables reached a record 72 days in August. They attributed worsening arrears to deteriorating company finances in a persistently weak economy, while noting the measure was not directly comparable with the government’s 60-day payment standard for large firms.

## Forward Market Significance

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Bangkok appearance is scheduled for October 16 at 03:30 UTC, or 11:30 p.m. Thursday in New York, after the completed U.S. bond session. It is the final major communication opportunity before Saturday’s blackout ahead of the October 27-28 meeting. The immediate question is whether strong producer prices and spending alter the patience Daly expressed, while declining yields and anxiety over AI investment change the balance of financial restraint. September PCE follows the policy decision, leaving officials to assess its likely composition before the complete release.

Friday’s September import- and export-price releases at 8:30 a.m. New York will extend the inflation picture. Consensus expects monthly increases of 0.8% and 1%, respectively, after 0.7% and 0.6%. Industrial production at 9:15 a.m. is expected to rise 0.4% after no change, with manufacturing production up 0.3% after a 0.3% decline and capacity utilization at 76.5% against 76.3%. Those results will put national output beside the sharp divergence between October’s New York and Philadelphia factory surveys.

Treasury’s Friday dealer questionnaire is the next communication on debt-management options ahead of November’s refunding. Thursday’s $6 billion long-maturity buyback gave the market an actual purchase operation; the survey may indicate whether officials are considering a change in future issuance. The September budget statement, expected Friday to show a $29 billion deficit after $167 billion, and August long-term TIC flows, with consensus at a $75.2 billion inflow after a $27.9 billion outflow, will add fiscal and cross-border demand information. The custody debate makes the composition and attribution of foreign holdings relevant alongside aggregate flows.

New World’s October 20 exchange deadline will establish final participation beyond the $189.1 million early tenders. CityFibre’s lender agreement remains the condition for owner financing, while Hain’s continuing asset-sale negotiations depend on resolving its debt maturity requirement. Qualtrics’ proposed return to syndication will test whether a smaller package and stronger protections can attract lenders while software exposure remains contested. FMC’s October 29 results and October 30 outlook will give creditors a fuller view of its pricing reset and financing needs.

The October 28 New Zealand decision and October 30 BOJ meeting arrive with officials supporting further tightening but preserving discretion over timing. France’s budget passage and potential Moody’s update remain more direct tests of sovereign confidence, with repo financing currently stable. In late-Thursday coverage, the EU was reported to be preparing broader powers that could close single-market access and examining import quotas in chemicals and machinery. Those prospective trade measures extend the dispute beyond the existing hybrid-car cap, adding another unresolved supply and pricing issue as central banks decide how far to tighten.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally as Asian technology losses deepen AI financing fears
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied after an overnight collapse in Asian technology shares intensified concern about AI financing and its implications for investment and growth. The 10-year yield fell 12.74 basis points to 5.058%, compared with a 5.93-basis-point decline in the 2-year to 4.7382%, narrowing the 2s10s spread by 6.81 basis points to 31.98. Lower real yields accounted for most of the move: the 10-year real yield fell 9.65 basis points to 2.7283%, while breakeven inflation declined 3.09 basis points to 2.3297%.

September PPI rose 1.3% and retail sales increased 0.8%, both above expectations, but interrupted the rally only briefly. Economists nevertheless lowered September PCE estimates based on relevant producer-price components. Mary Daly favored further tightening without an immediate move; swaps still anticipated another increase by year-end. Municipal bonds also rallied, with the benchmark 10-year yield down 16 basis points to 3.74% at 4 p.m. New York.

The S&P 500 recovered to a gain, and CoreWeave shares rose 5.9% after Nvidia’s Jensen Huang defended its finances. CoreWeave’s 5-year protection cost nevertheless reached an intraday record of 1,194.5 basis points, against more than $40 billion of debt and increasingly negative free cash flow. FMC’s 2031 bonds traded around a 10.5% yield after a pricing overhaul, while CityFibre sought creditor concessions and Hain weighed Chapter 11. Broad U.S. high-yield spreads finished modestly tighter, underscoring the gap between the recovery in government bonds and individual borrowers’ ability to refinance.
